assumptions: Only conservative visually observed contact intervals may receive conditional ground force. Unreviewed, occluded and candidate frames do not.
The source sole point is the lower visible heel/toe landmark in the native image; it is approximate, can roll or drift, and is not a measured pressure center.
The target sole is an assumed world-down offset of 2.5 percent of target height from the ankle. No foot angle, foot mass or sole mesh is estimated.
Wall registration only co-registers image evidence. It does not calibrate floor metric distances. All ground support stays geometry-uncertain.
Ground normal is assumed model image-up. The configurable foot friction coefficient applies equally to ground and hold feet.
Floor polygons are manually estimated native-image regions interpolated between keyframes, not automatic wall/floor segmentation.
Ground observations stop at frame 74. Later unreviewed free limbs never acquire ground support by default.
Walking, rolling and lift-off are dynamic. The current solver remains quasi-static and does not prove no-slip or dynamic feasibility.
Fit weight 0.8 is an objective weight, not a calibrated contact probability; original classifier confidences remain unchanged.

Left shoe clearly separated from floor; wall/hold status is still the original model prediction.

Foot above floor / moving onto wall hold; this does not itself confirm a particular hold.

method: One full-sequence sparse-direct bounded pose/force optimization per IRLS iteration, in COM coordinates, with exact nominal singleton support constraints and soft contact restoration.

limitations: Soft global objectives seek improved poses; convergence is not a global optimum or physical validation.
Prospective COM intervals assume desired contacts can be reached; final audits independently exclude missed holds.
IRLS favors achievable contacts and can increase errors on incompatible contacts; all original targets remain audited.
Support confidence and calibration are unchanged; conditional support never becomes confirmed evidence.
Contact labels/timing stay fixed. Direct hold changes retain timing uncertainty; ground support is not invented.
Unloading encourages a gradual reduction in departing candidate force and fixed-pose reserve without departing limbs.
The final pre-release candidate load is flagged above 1% body weight; counterfactual readiness is a separate check.
Assumed 2D quasi-static force capacities/friction omit depth, inertia, measured normals, grip strength and joint torques.
Temporal penalties and motion limits do not establish dynamic feasibility. Unresolved constraints remain visible.
